title: 第 35 課｜歐拉角：用三個角度描述剛體的方向｜Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學
description:
剛體的位置由質心的三個座標，加上三個決定方向的角度描述，最常用的一組就是歐拉角。因為只關心座標軸之間的夾角，我們把固定座標系 X、Y、Z 與隨物體轉的座標系 x₁、x₂、x₃ 的原點放在一起。物體的 x₁x₂ 平面與固定的 XY 平面交出一條直線 ON，稱為節線；它同時垂直於 Z 與 x₃，正方向取成 z × x₃。三個歐拉角是：θ 為 Z 與 x₃ 的夾角，範圍 0 到 π；φ 從 X 量到節線；ψ 從節線量到 x₁，後兩者分別繞 Z 與 x₃ 依右手螺旋方向量，範圍 0 到 2π。因此任何方向都可由三次接續的轉動得到：先繞 Z 轉 φ，再繞節線轉 θ，最後繞 x₃ 轉 ψ。把角速度拆成沿節線的 dθ/dt、沿 Z 的 dφ/dt 與沿 x₃ 的 dψ/dt 三份（這三根軸並不互相垂直），再各自投影到物體的三根軸上，就得到 Ω₁ = (dφ/dt) sinθ sinψ + (dθ/dt) cosψ、Ω₂ = (dφ/dt) sinθ cosψ − (dθ/dt) sinψ、Ω₃ = (dφ/dt) cosθ + dψ/dt。若三根軸取成慣性主軸，對稱陀螺的轉動動能就是 T = ½ I₁ [ (dθ/dt)² + (dφ/dt)² sin²θ ] + ½ I₃ [ (dφ/dt) cosθ + dψ/dt ]²。利用對稱陀螺可任選垂直於 x₃ 的兩根主軸這個自由度，把 x₁ 取在節線上使 ψ = 0，分量便化簡成 Ω₁ = dθ/dt、Ω₂ = (dφ/dt) sinθ、Ω₃ = (dφ/dt) cosθ + dψ/dt。用它重算對稱陀螺的自由轉動：取 Z 沿守恆的角動量，由於 x₁ 垂直於 M，三個分量為 M₁ = 0、M₂ = M sinθ、M₃ = M cosθ；比較兩組式子立刻得到 dθ/dt = 0、dφ/dt = M / I₁、Ω₃ = ( M / I₃ ) cosθ，正是第 33 課用幾何得到的規則進動。影片用一張軸測投影圖貫穿全課，包含三次轉動的循環動畫、角速度三分量的即時堆疊長條圖，以及最後掃出圓錐的規則進動。

本影片為《Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學》教學系列第 35 課（繁體中文版）。

title: Lesson 35 | Eulerian Angles: Three Angles for the Orientation of a Rigid Body | Landau–Lifshitz
description:
The position of a rigid body is fixed by three coordinates for its centre of mass plus three angles for its orientation, and the most convenient set is the Eulerian angles. Since only the angles between the axes matter, we let the fixed frame X, Y, Z and the body frame x₁, x₂, x₃ share one origin. The body's x₁x₂ plane cuts the fixed XY plane along a straight line ON, the line of nodes; it is perpendicular to both Z and x₃, with positive direction along z × x₃. The three angles are θ, between Z and x₃, running from 0 to π; φ, from X to the line of nodes; and ψ, from the line of nodes to x₁, the last two measured about Z and about x₃ by the corkscrew rule, from 0 to 2π. Any orientation is therefore reached by three successive rotations: φ about Z, then θ about the line of nodes, then ψ about x₃. Splitting the angular velocity into dθ/dt along the line of nodes, dφ/dt along the fixed Z and dψ/dt along x₃ — three axes that are not mutually perpendicular — and projecting each onto the body axes gives Ω₁ = (dφ/dt) sinθ sinψ + (dθ/dt) cosψ, Ω₂ = (dφ/dt) sinθ cosψ − (dθ/dt) sinψ, and Ω₃ = (dφ/dt) cosθ + dψ/dt. If those axes are the principal axes of inertia, the rotational energy of a symmetrical top is T = ½ I₁ [ (dθ/dt)² + (dφ/dt)² sin²θ ] + ½ I₃ [ (dφ/dt) cosθ + dψ/dt ]². Since the two principal axes across the symmetry axis may be chosen freely, putting x₁ on the line of nodes makes ψ = 0 and the components collapse to Ω₁ = dθ/dt, Ω₂ = (dφ/dt) sinθ, Ω₃ = (dφ/dt) cosθ + dψ/dt. Redoing the free motion of a symmetrical top with Z along the conserved angular momentum, x₁ is perpendicular to M so the components are M₁ = 0, M₂ = M sinθ, M₃ = M cosθ. Comparing the two sets gives dθ/dt = 0, dφ/dt = M / I₁ and Ω₃ = ( M / I₃ ) cosθ — exactly the regular precession found geometrically in lesson 33. Animated in one axonometric picture, with a looping three-rotation sequence, live stacked bars for the three components, and the cone swept out at the end.

Lesson 35 of the Landau–Lifshitz Classical Mechanics teaching series (English edition).
